name: How much contingency should I keep for a custom kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I keep for a custom kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I keep for a custom kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency reserve is essential in any custom kitchen remodel because demolition often reveals issues that were not visible during planning. In Los Angeles, older homes frequently contain outdated wiring, plumbing problems, uneven floors, or prior patchwork that must be corrected before the new kitchen goes in. Homeowners should keep a separate contingency rather than spending the full budget on design choices up front. The reserve helps cover repairs, upgrades, and small scope changes without forcing the project to stall. It also protects against product substitution when a selected item becomes unavailable and a comparable replacement costs more. The exact amount depends on age of the home, scope of structural changes, and complexity of the design, but the key is to treat contingency as required, not optional. Projects with wall removal, custom millwork, or major system updates should have a more generous reserve than simple cosmetic updates.
